_comment: Carry destination for the next #3885 group: the CI-cost levers the light-grading
pull request (handoff/ci-3885-nonprod-scope) measured and left open. Shape and
stage: the next #3885 group: CI cost of grading a head twice, after light grading

carries.from: the #3885 light-grading pull request (handoff/ci-3885-nonprod-scope): its `## Figures` measured duplicate verified dispatches with dev/audit/harnesses/ci3885_light.py (at 7eb9b2fd81bbe71be048e730481470de62c0932c) dup
carries.control: Established by measurement with its null control. `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/ci3885_light.py (at 7eb9b2fd81bbe71be048e730481470de62c0932c) dup 2026-11-21` counted 28 of 38 PR-naming ci.yml workflow_dispatch runs (17,495 runner-min) created after a pull_request run at the same head had completed with a conclusion other than cancelled, action_required or skipped; the other 10 (5,666 runner-min) were their head's sole grader. Null control: the same arm on 2026-11-24 counts 0 of 0, and on 2026-11-23 2 of 6 (304 runner-min), so the arm does not read every dispatch as a duplicate. Unit sets were not compared: 17,495 is an upper bound on what reuse saves, against 5,189 runner-min the light stand-downs saved on that day's dispatches.
carries.remeasure: Do not trust the counts: they are 2026-11-21's, and that day predates CI-2 (verified dispatch scoped by the three-dot list, 2eea9dc559). Re-run `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/ci3885_light.py (at 7eb9b2fd81bbe71be048e730481470de62c0932c) dup DAY` for a busy day after your merge base, and compare each duplicate's unit set (tools/ci/prelude.py outputs) against its earlier pull_request run's before counting it.
carries.brief: First find why a verified dispatch was fired at a head a pull_request run had already graded (the dispatcher's own trigger, read from tools/audit/seat/ and tools/pr/), because stopping the redundant dispatch at its source may need no CI change at all. Only if the dispatch is needed, make a dispatch whose head carries a concluded pull_request run with the same unit set reuse that run's verdict: tools/ci/gate.py would then accept another run's job conclusions as this run's required contexts, which is a trust-model change and needs a design (decision 0014) before a fixer. Carry: #3885

carries.from: the #3885 light-grading pull request (handoff/ci-3885-nonprod-scope): its `## Forward-carry`, on the env_drift cache after a light push
carries.control: Measured by the #3885 L4 pull request (handoff/r11-ci-3885-queue-l4), GitHub MCP job listings and logs: light push fd93aa3e9b (CI run 45907525407, tests / fast 3/4, the shard owning tests/env_drift.py) scoped env_drift out (`SKIP  tests/env_drift.py`) and its warmed-cache save logged `Path(s) specified in the action for caching do(es) not exist, hence no cache is being saved`. The first pull request run forked at that commit (run 45907841043, PR 3845, tests / fast 3/4) logged `Cache not found for input keys: drift-baseline-fe12a5...` and ran `env_drift.py --all fd93aa3e9b` cold in 262 s. The cache is read by pull requests, not by the next push (a push restores no drift entry), so the remeasure clause's push-log reading cannot show it. Null control not separated: run 45818958831 (PR 3870), forked at full push 1d3077736d whose push run was still running, also saved a fresh entry (a miss, 326 s); a miss after a full push whose run had saved is still owed, and so is the hit duration that prices the miss.
carries.remeasure: Read the `fast` job logs of the first push run on main after this pull request merges whose range reaches tests/env_drift.py, and the one before it, and record hit or miss for the env_drift cache in each, with their run ids.
carries.brief: A light push never warms the drift-baseline cache, so each pull request whose run forks at it and reaches tests/env_drift.py pays a cold `--all` capture (262 s measured, before the hit duration is subtracted). Measure the hit duration and the count of such forks per day, and if the cold captures cost more than carrying the range base's entry forward on a light push, carry it forward the way tests.yml's coverage job carries its range base's per-script entry on a stood-down push; env_drift's in-entry key re-check refuses an entry restored under another commit's key, so the carry re-keys it rather than copies it. Carry: #3885

carries.from: the #3885 item 2 pull request (handoff/r11-outside-ci-3885-sampling): its `## Figures` wall-time and census, dev/audit/harnesses/ci3885_sampling.py
carries.control: Measured at the re-recorded table (recorded_at ac9045c223): tests/entities.py run whole took 612.6 s and run sampled over #3936's file list 588.2 s and 619.6 s (61 of 65 spans: 2 diff, 1 edited, 13 forward, 10 sample, 35 needed), so the 30% draw saves less than the run-to-run spread. Null control: with the same seed the plan prints 61 of 65 spans and the whole run 65 section headings, so the draw does thin the set; `needs` puts the dropped spans back. `ci3885_sampling.py census 30` over main's last 30 merges: no scoped plan for either script ran under 0.97 of the recorded span seconds.
carries.remeasure: Re-run `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/ci3885_sampling.py census 30` and the wall pair (`python3 tests/entities.py` against `python3 tests/case_select.py run tests/entities.py --sample --seed <N>-<sha> --files <list>`) at your own merge base after P2a and P2b land; do not carry these seconds.
carries.brief: The design note on design/r11-ci-3885-rest (f139601cee) stop rule holds: sampling alone saves nothing until the omnibus span is split (P2a) and `needs` is tightened (P2b). Those parts own the gain; item 2's plan, draw, seed and routing are on main for them to reuse, and `plan()` already applies rules (i)-(v), so P2d's rule (i) and (iii) are built and P2d is the soundness replay and the measurement table. Carry: #3885

carries.from: the #3885 item 2 pull request (handoff/r11-outside-ci-3885-sampling): the table's header_hash arm
carries.control: At ac9045c223 the table recorded at f184477ba8 matched neither script's header (`python3 tests/case_select.py plan tests/entities.py --seed 1-<sha> --files <list>` printed FULL, the header's text differs), after 236 commits touching the two scripts; re-recorded at ac9045c223 the same command plans SCOPED. A header edit (one import line moved each header) therefore turns sampling off until the next Linux re-record.
carries.remeasure: Count the commits touching either script's header between two recordings with `git log` over the header line range `case_select.py split` prints.
carries.brief: P3 (closures-autofix and CASE UNDER-SCOPED) must also re-record an entry whose header_hash moved, as a replacement on Linux, or every plan reads FULL from the first header edit after a recording. Carry: #3885

carries.from: the #3885 item 2 pull request (handoff/r11-outside-ci-3885-sampling): its fail-safe arms beyond the approved list
carries.control: tests/case_select.py `plan` refuses to scope when a changed unit is in the header's recorded reads (other than the script itself), or is in the script's tests/closures.json closure and in no span's recording; each arm has a self-test row and a mutant in `ci3885_sampling.py mutants` that the self-test kills. The census shows the header arm firing on every production merge in the window (the headers read 82 and 93 custom_components files).
carries.remeasure: `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/ci3885_sampling.py census 30`: count the FULL lines naming `the header reads`.
carries.brief: A production diff is FULL for the two scripts by these arms, since a span can read state the header built from a changed module without recording that module. Narrowing them (per-name header provenance) belongs with P2b's needs work and needs the soundness replay before it lands. Carry: #3885
